The *Micchādiṭṭhika Sutta* (Iti 70; PTS It 58) is a discourse found in the third division of the *Itivuttaka*. In this sutta, titled "Having Wrong View" (*Micchādiṭṭhikasutta*), the Buddha testifies that he has personally seen beings reborn into states of woe, unhappy destinations, perdition, and hell in accordance with their wrong views, bodily and verbal misconduct, and abuse of noble ones.

The descriptive formula describing beings reborn according to their kamma and views also shares long textual segments (§§2.1–3.1 and §§4.1–4.2) with prominent discourses in the Four Nikāyas, including the *Devadūta Sutta* (MN 130), the *Mahāsīhanāda Sutta* (MN 12), the *Sāmaññaphala Sutta* (DN 2), the *Dasakanipāta* of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 10), and the *Nidāna Saṁyutta* (SN 12) [DharmaNexus].
